sentences.text: Physogaleus was an extinct genus of small requiem sharks belonging to the family Carcharhinidae and the class Chondrichthyes.
Scientists know this animal only from fossil teeth and isolated vertebrae.
Its teeth were smaller than those of true tiger sharks and lacked the heavy serrations found in Galeocerdo.
Physogaleus appears in the BBC book adaptation Monsters of the Sea, a spin-off of Walking with Dinosaurs.
In the story, the shark attempts to steal a Basilosaurus kill but fails.
The genus Physogaleus was established by Cappetta in 1980.
Physogaleus likely ate bony fish and probably grew to about 3 meters in length.
This shark lived from the Thanetian to the Gelasian, between 59.24 and 1.8 million years ago.
Researchers created the genus Physogaleus because species within it were more morphologically similar to each other than to the genus Galeocerdo.
